CIVCM 211N: Through readings, discussion, deliberation, listening, and individual as well as collaborative action, this course gives students the opportunity to learn about and practice theories and habits of civic and community engagement and public scholarship with the goal of helping to build democratic capacity and sustain participatory democracy.
CIVCM 494: Supervised student activities on research projects identified on an individual basis.
CIVCM 495: Supervised off-campus, nongroup instruction including field experiences, practica, or internships.
